narrative.text: You are at the podium for a live press conference. The lights are hot, the cameras are rolling. A reporter asks a question about the economy. As you turn to address him, the nerve damage in your hand flares up violently. Your arm spasms, knocking your water glass off the podium with a loud crash. The room goes silent.
Chancellor, are you feeling unwell? The nation is watching. There are rumors that the assassination attempt left you with permanent damage. Is that true?

The cameras are zooming in. The water is pooling on the floor. My hand is still shaking. I can feel the ringing in my ear drowning out the room. I have to say something, or this will be the only story in tomorrow's papers.

choices.text: Admit the injury. 'The attempt on my life left scars. I govern with them.'
Lie. 'I am simply exhausted from working for the Republic.'
Attack the reporter. 'How dare you question my health while Veltrians are starving?'
